transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

That light usually does not mean the removable container itself is full. On Bosch condenser/heat-pump dryers it can also mean condensate water is backing up in the bottom sump/pump area because lint or debris is blocking it, or the float/pump sensor is stuck.

Try this:

1. Switch off and unplug the dryer.
2. Empty the container once more, then rinse it and check the valve/opening where it slides into the machine isn’t blocked by fluff.
3. Clean both lint filters thoroughly (usually in the door). Wash them under warm water if they look coated, then let them dry fully. A nearly invisible film from detergent/fabric softener can restrict airflow.
4. Check the lower filter/service flap at the bottom front, if your model has one. Remove lint carefully and wipe out any standing water you can reach with a cloth.
• Do not force out the heat exchanger on models marked SelfCleaning Condenser unless the manual specifically says it is removable.
5. If it has a drain hose connected to plumbing, check that it is not kinked, blocked, or pushed too far down the standpipe.
6. Leave it unplugged for around 10 minutes, then try a short timed programme.

If the warning returns quickly, especially after the machine has run for a few minutes, the likely causes are:
• blocked condensate pump/sump,
• stuck float switch,
• failed condensate pump,
• blockage in the internal hose leading to the tank.

Those usually need the lower pump area cleaned or serviced. Avoid repeatedly restarting it, as water can accumulate inside the base.

If you send the Bosch E-Nr/model number from the sticker around the door opening (for example, `WTW...` or `WTH...`), I can give model-specific cleaning/access instructions.

Right, did all that. Container rinsed and the sieve was slimy so I cleaned it, both filters cleaned (fairly clean), no drain hose fitted. Found a small cover at the bottom with grey slimy water and fluff behind it, wiped what I could reach. It ran about 60 mins this time but the light came on again. Model on the manual cover just starts WTG8, the full label is on the back and I can't get at it as it's stacked on the washer.

The fact it now runs for about an hour before stopping strongly suggests the internal condensate sump is filling but the pump cannot clear it fast enough. The grey slimy water/fluff behind that lower cover is a good clue: sludge has likely reached the pump well, its float switch, or the small hose leading up to the water container.

On a Bosch WTG8 condenser dryer, that is usually beyond the normal lint-filter cleaning and often needs the pump/sump area opened and cleaned properly. Possible faults are:

• lint/slime blocking the condensate pump inlet or internal hose;
• float sensor sticking in the “full” position;
• weak or failed condensate pump.

I would avoid continuing to reset and run it repeatedly — eventually the water can accumulate in the base and potentially leak or trip the appliance.

A couple of safe final checks:

• With it unplugged, use a torch through the lower service opening and remove only loose fluff/sludge you can easily reach; a turkey baster/sponge can remove accessible dirty water.
• Do not poke tools deep inside, pull on hoses, or pour water/cleaner into the opening.
• Do not tip the dryer while it is stacked.

The model/E-Nr may also be on the inside of the door opening or around the door frame, not only at the rear. Look for a sticker beginning something like `E-Nr WTG8.../..`; a phone photo may help.

But based on what you’ve already done, I’d book an appliance engineer and describe it as: “Bosch WTG8 condenser dryer: empty-container warning despite empty tank; grey sludge/water in lower condenser area; runs roughly 60 minutes then stops — suspect condensate pump/sump blockage or float.” That should direct them to the relevant area rather than just telling you to clean filters again.
